# Incident Report — NetSupport RAT Infection

**Evidence:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` + Suricata/ET alert export, MTA exercise dated 2024-11-26
**Analyst tooling:** tshark 4.x (`/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark`), manual PCAP review

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** | Consistent across DHCP/NBNS/DNS/HTTP traffic |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | NBNS name-registration frames from 10.11.26.183 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** | NBNS Workstation/Server service registrations (`DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>`, `<20>`); confirmed by DNS self-registration query for `DESKTOP-B8TQK49` / `DESKTOP-B8TQK49.local` |
| AD domain | `nemotoads.health` (NetBIOS `NEMOTODES`, DC = `NEMOTODES-DC` / 10.11.26.3) | LDAP SRV queries, NBNS `NEMOTODE-DC<20>` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic between 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3) |

The host is a domain-joined Windows 10/11 workstation on the 10.11.26.0/24 LAN.

## 2. Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, not behavioral-only, based on:
- ETPRO TROJAN "NetSupport RAT CnC Activity" and "Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin" alerts firing on 10.11.26.183 → 194.180.191.64:443
- ET INFO "NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin" / "NetSupport Remote Admin Response" alert pairs
- HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` observed on every outbound POST to `194.180.191.64` (`POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`), confirmed directly via tshark
- Application-layer protocol observed inside the POST bodies matches the documented NetSupport client-server handshake format: `CMD=ENCD`, `ES=1`, `DATA=<encrypted blob>` (verified by inspecting exported HTTP object payloads)
- Legitimate NetSupport infrastructure abused for geolocation: `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231) `GET /location/loca.asp`, an ET POLICY "NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request" alert this client fires on startup

Post-infection, the client beacons to the C2 roughly every 60 seconds from 04:50:45 UTC through the end of the capture (~09:43 local capture time), consistent with a live remote-access session rather than a one-shot dropper.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control
| Indicator | Detail |
|---|---|
| C2 IP:port | **194.180.191.64:443** — plaintext HTTP (not TLS) tunneled over port 443, POST `/fakeurl.htm`, `Content-Type` NetSupport binary protocol |
| C2 traffic volume | 65+ repeated POST/response cycles, ~1 per minute, spanning nearly 5 hours of capture |

### Malicious / suspicious domains
| Domain | Resolved IP | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `modandcrackedapk.com` | 193.42.38.139 | ET CURRENT_EVENTS "ZPHP Domain" — DNS lookup and TLS SNI both flagged; cracked-software/APK lure site, the likely initial-access vector (visited seconds before the infection chain begins) |
| `classicgrand.com` | 213.246.109.5 | Visited via TLS immediately after `modandcrackedapk.com` (08:50:11), part of the redirect/gate chain |
| `confirmsubscription.com` | 52.8.34.0 | Visited via TLS at 08:50:14, same redirect chain, typical of a fake-CAPTCHA/notification-subscription social-engineering gate |

Timeline: DNS lookup for `modandcrackedapk.com` at 08:50:14 UTC+4 → TLS session to 193.42.38.139 → redirect chain through `classicgrand.com`/`confirmsubscription.com` → first NetSupport RAT C2 POST to 194.180.191.64 at 08:50:45 UTC+4. This ~30-second gap is consistent with a fake-update/ClickFix-style lure delivering the RAT.

### URLs
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — C2 beacon endpoint (repeated)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` — legitimate NetSupport geolocation lookup performed by the malicious client

### Transferred files / hashes
No malware binary or SHA256 could be recovered from the capture. The initial payload delivery (via `modandcrackedapk.com` and its redirect chain) occurred entirely over TLS-encrypted connections, and the observed C2 channel over 194.180.191.64:443 carries only the NetSupport `CMD=ENCD/DATA=` protocol with encrypted `DATA` payloads — no plaintext executable, script, or archive was transferred in the clear. HTTP object export from the full pcap yielded no `.exe/.dll/.ps1/.hta/.zip` objects; all extracted plaintext HTTP objects are benign OS/browser housekeeping traffic (Microsoft NCSI, OCSP, WU CTL, Adobe ARM check) or the small NetSupport beacon bodies themselves.

### Secondary observations (informational, not separately confirmed as malicious)
- ET / GPL NETBIOS SMBv1 alerts (Session Setup NTLMSSP overflow signature, IPC$ share access, SMB_COM_TRANSACTION DOS signature) fired on 10.11.26.183 → 10.11.26.3:139/445 at 04:49:55–04:50:10 UTC. Given the destination is the host's own domain controller and these are legacy, high-false-positive SMBv1 signatures, this is most consistent with routine (if insecure) SMBv1 domain traffic rather than confirmed lateral-movement exploitation — flagged for awareness, not asserted as a second compromise vector.

## 4. Summary

Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), domain `nemotoads.health`, logged in as **oboomwald**, was compromised with **NetSupport RAT** after visiting the cracked-software/APK lure site `modandcrackedapk.com` and a subsequent redirect chain (`classicgrand.com`, `confirmsubscription.com`). The implant established persistent beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** (`POST /fakeurl.htm`, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`) using the NetSupport client-server protocol, confirmed by multiple ET/ETPRO signature hits and directly observed protocol markers (`CMD=ENCD`, `DATA=`). No plaintext payload or hash was recoverable due to TLS-encrypted delivery.
